runs.name: corpus_full:groovy
runs.note: Measured over EVERY tracked .groovy file in the corpus (git ls-files '*.groovy', 7,114 files, 0 failures), single process, 20-file warm-up, $HOME/fixtures/xml/repos/grails-core. This REPLACES the 400-file 'corpus_subset' run, which is removed rather than kept: it reported 110 files/s against the full corpus's measured 14 files/s, so keeping both would have left a number 8x optimistic in the record. The gap is not the analyzer being slower on more data -- the first files parsed are the shallow modules, and grails-data-* / grails-web-* are both larger and deeper, so the subset was sampling the cheap end. Any budget read against 110 files/s is void.

note: Complexity envelope per analyzer: wall time, symbols/s, relationships/s, peak RSS. Budgets are declared per analyzer in docs/analyzers/. 'corpus_subset' was a 400-file sample and has been replaced by a full-corpus run; see runs[].note for why the two disagree.
